explanation: An empirical formula is the simplest whole-number ratio of atoms in a compound. Starting from mass percents, you assume a 100 g sample so each percent equals grams, divide each element's grams by its molar mass to get moles, then divide every mole value by the smallest of them to expose the ratio. Rounding those ratios to whole numbers gives the empirical formula; the molecular formula is then a whole-number multiple of it (found from the actual molar mass). This CxHyOz demo highlights each element's percent, moles, and scaled ratio, the exact workflow AP free-response problems reward.
bullets: Assume a 100 g sample so mass% reads directly as grams.
Divide grams by molar mass to get moles of each element.
Divide all mole values by the smallest to get the ratio.
Round ratios to whole numbers: that IS the empirical formula.
